<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />&c., and also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=5}}, &c. Similarly the article is used with terms of measurement, as {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֵפָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=36}}, &c.: {{GHGheb|text=הַחֹמֶר}} and {{GHGheb|text=הַבַּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָעֹ֫מֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּחֶ֫בֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=2}}.

(''c'') The expression of abstract ideas of every kind, since they are likewise used to represent whole classes of attributes or states, physical or moral defects, &c.; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=בַּצֶּ֫דֶק}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=11}} ''and they smote the men''... {{GHGheb|text=בַּסַּנְוֵרִים|translate=with blindness}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=9}}, &c.; but in {{GHGheb|text=הַח֫שֶׁךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=2}} the article is no doubt due to dittography of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, and the parallel {{GHGheb|text=וַֽעֲרָפֶל}} has no article.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|o}}
(''d'') ''Comparisons'', since the object compared is treated not (as usually in English) individually but as a general term, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=18}} ''white'' {{GHGheb|text=כַּשֶּׁ֫לֶג|translate=as snow}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּצֶּ֫מֶר|translate=as wool}}; ''red'' {{GHGheb|text=כַּתּוֹלָע|translate=like crimson}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=4}} ''and the heavens shall be rolled together'' {{GHGheb|text=כַּסֵּפֶר|translate=as a scroll}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=9|hidebook=1}} ''as'' {{GHGheb|text=פְּתִיל־הַנְּעֹרֶת|translate=a string of tow is broken}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=15|hidebook=1}}; cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=6}}, where the object compared is determined by a determinate genitive which follows (according to {{GHGpar|127|a}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|p}}
Examples of indeterminate comparisons are rare, and perhaps due only to the Masora,—so at least in the case of singulars, while in such plurals as those in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=4}}, 7, the omission of the article may be explained by the ordinary rules. On the other hand, the article is regularly omitted when the object compared is already defined by means of an attribute (or relative clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=12}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּעוֹף נוֹדֵד קֵן מְשֻׁלָּח|translate=as wandering birds}}, (as) ''a scattered nest'' (but cf. 10:14 {{GHGheb|text=כַּקֵּן}}); 14:19, 29:5 {{GHGheb|text=כְּמֹץ עֹבֵר}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=1|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּמֹּץ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=14|hidebook=1}}.—In comparisons with persons also the Masora seems to avoid the use of the article, as in {{GHGheb|text=כְּגִבּוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=14}} and seven other places ({{GHGheb|text=כַּגִּכּוֹר}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=13}}), {{GHGheb|text=כְּאָב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=18}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּגֶ֫בֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=7|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|q}}
'''4.''' Peculiar to Hebrew<ref>Cf., however, analogous examples in biblical Aramaic in Kautzsch’s {{GHGcite|title=Gramm. des Bibl. Aram.}}, 79 f, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=2|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=3|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, &c.</ref> is the employment of the article to denote a single person or thing (primarily one which is as yet unknown, and therefore not capable of being defined) as being present to the mind under given circumstances. In such cases in English the indefinite article is mostly used.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|r}}
Thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=19}} ''as if a man did flee from a lion'' ({{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֲרִי}}, i.e. the particular lion pursuing him at the time), ''and a bear'' ({{GHGheb|text=הַדֹּב}}) ''met him'', &c., cf. 3:12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=36}} (John 10:12); also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}} f., 14:13 ({{GHGheb|text=הַפָּלִיט}}, i.e. ''one that had escaped'', the particular one who came just then; so also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=21|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=13}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=1}}, 11 18:7 ''the servant'', who is regarded as being constantly at hand and awaiting his commands; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=17}} (but {{GHGheb|text=הַנַּ֫עַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=27}} is used like {{GHGheb|text=הַפָּלִיט}} above); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=30}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=בַּמְּעָרָה}} means in ''the'' well-known ''cave''; {{GHGheb|text=בַּמָּקוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=11}}, according to Dillmann, upon ''the'' place suitable for passing the night, or the right place, but it may possibly also refer to ''the'' sanctuary of Bethel afterwards so sacred and celebrated; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=20|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=21}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=23|verse=42}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=10|hidebook=1}} (Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרְאֵלִי}} without the article); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, 9, 25:6, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (? most<section end=par126 /><noinclude>
